findings.summary: The present-tense installability statement in docs/project-status.md and docs/release/build-and-release.md is forward-looking: at HEAD 266ad46 origin/main (09596e0) predates manifest.json and no v1.0.1 GitHub release asset exists, so a catalog install cannot yet succeed; the surrounding text marks Phase 8 in progress and the release as a pending manual step, so this is accepted as a by-design sequencing reference (same class as the accepted finding 8.1-R2).
findings.detail: docs/project-status.md lines 5-7 read '... ArrTags is installable through the standard Jellyfin plugin catalog from the public repository benssson/ArrTags ...; the GitHub release and asset upload remain a manual user step', and docs/release/build-and-release.md line 207-213 says 'ArrTags is installable ... Jellyfin is pointed at the raw manifest URL'. I verified the repository state: git rev-parse origin/main = 09596e0 ('record phase 6 completion tag'), HEAD = 266ad46 is 29 commits ahead, and `git cat-file -e origin/main:manifest.json` fails, so the raw main manifest URL is not live and the manifest sourceUrl asset (releases/download/v1.0.1/ArrTags_1.0.1.0.zip) does not exist. The statement is therefore not literally true yet. It is not a stale release-identity claim (no current surface presents 0.1.0.0 as current), it matches the PLANS.md Phase 8 goal wording ('make ArrTags installable ...'), and the task 8.1 reviewer accepted the identical sequencing forward reference as 8.1-R2. No action required for task 8.5; a future reconciliation could qualify the tense.
evidence: docs/project-status.md:5-11 -> 'Phase 8 -- Release distribution is in progress (tasks 8.1-8.5 complete; task 8.6 pending): ArrTags is installable ...; the GitHub release and asset upload remain a manual user step'
docs/release/build-and-release.md:207-213 -> 'ArrTags is installable through the standard Jellyfin plugin catalog ... raw manifest URL'
git rev-parse origin/main -> 09596e0; git rev-list --count origin/main..HEAD -> 29; git cat-file -e origin/main:manifest.json -> fatal: not in origin/main
manifest.json versions[0].sourceUrl -> https://github.com/benssson/ArrTags/releases/download/v1.0.1/ArrTags_1.0.1.0.zip (asset not published; user manual step)
findings.recommended_action: None required for task 8.5. If the paragraph is later edited, qualify the claim (for example 'Phase 8 makes ArrTags installable ... once the pending repository push and GitHub release publication complete').

findings.summary: docs/limitations.md P1 says byte-identity of the 1.0.1.0 artifact 'is demonstrated with the pinned toolchain', but the cross-export reproducibility matrix was re-run only for 0.1.0; the 1.0.1.0 evidence is repeated same-tree package stability, which P1's own notes disclose, so it is not an overclaim.
findings.detail: P1 (lines 227-250) records the current 1.0.1.0 identity and states 'Byte-identity ... is demonstrated with the pinned toolchain', then explicitly adds 'no automated test guards byte-reproducibility ... reproducibility is verified by re-running ./build.sh package and comparing SHA-256' and 'the current 1.0.1.0 artifact is byte-stable across repeated ./build.sh package runs (the Phase 8 task 8.4 and 8.5 runs produced the identical SHA-256)'. docs/release/build-and-release.md labels the two-clean-export reproducibility matrix as '0.1.0 history' and the worker report known_limitations acknowledges the full matrix was not re-run at 1.0.1.0. I independently rebuilt with `. /config/arrtags-env.sh && ./build.sh package` and reproduced the recorded SHA-256/MD5/size, so the repeated-run stability claim is true. The doc is transparent about what was verified, so no action is required.
findings.recommended_action: None required; a future task could state the 1.0.1.0 reproducibility evidence scope explicitly.
